text: Every engineering organization already knows why its payments service
failed last time. That knowledge is sitting in a
postmortem nobody reads, a Slack thread nobody can find,
and one engineer's head.
So when an AI agent shows up to change
something, it starts from zero — and repeats the
outage you already had.
OrgMemory is the memory layer for engineering organizations.
It turns your postmortems, Slack, and repos into a
time-aware memory graph where every fact cites its evidence.
And through WebMCP, the authenticated page itself registers twenty-one
browser-native tools, so any agent working here can ask
what the company knows before it acts, using the
page's own session. The agent never sees a credential.
Here's the tool this product exists for: get_orgmemory_briefing.
Every other retrieval tool answers a question.
This one answers an intent: "I'm about to do
this thing." Watch. The agent says what it's about
to do... and OrgMemory comes back with a verdict:
requires approval. Two prior incidents that started exactly this
way. The decision to cap worker concurrency that constrains
it. The blast radius — payments shares a Postgres
cluster with the ledger.
And the remembered first-response procedure.
Every line carries a memory ID a person can
open. And no model runs in this path.
Ask twice, get the same verdict twice.
An agent about to restart production needs a control,
not a summary. And the boundary is real, not
decorative: a read-only intent comes back, "proceed."
But OrgMemory will not approve it for you.
Three permission tiers, legible to an agent from the
annotations alone. Reads are permission-trimmed server-side against your team
scope. An outcome report appends to a ledger and
changes no knowledge. And the only path for a
single fact into company memory is a proposal a
human approves. Capability is never authorization.
Serving that briefing opened a row in the outcome
ledger. After acting — from GitHub, PagerDuty, wherever —
the agent closes it with record_orgmemory_outcome: what it did,
and whether it worked.
Context served. Action taken.
Outcome observed. That record — which context actually produced
correct action inside this company — is the one
asset a better model cannot copy.
And it compounds with every run.
Twenty-one browser-native tools. An agent that gets briefed before
it acts, and reports back after.
OrgMemory. Your organization remembers.
